ruling.recommended_action: Refund $4.08 excess distance fare to the rider's original payment method; issue the driver a notification-duty reminder and log the notification failure on his route-compliance record (no formal warning — first incident)
ruling.reasoning:
Route deviation, rider-filed. GPS shows 13.5 km actual vs 10.6 km optimal, a deviation of +2.9 km [F1], well over the 1 km tolerance (RD-1). The code isolates one off-route segment, 08:59–09:06, where 4.50 km was driven against 1.92 km optimal, +2.58 km [F3].

Was that segment exempt? Two possible grounds fail. (a) Traffic (RD-4): the only bad band is Ayer Rajah Expressway (band 2) [F10], but the AYE is not on the recommended route nor the part of it replaced; the recommended roads were flowing (CXE band 7, Kent Ridge band 5) [F11][F12] and no incident is recorded anywhere near the route [F13]. A traffic reason on an unrelated road does not exempt the segment. (b) Rider consent (RD-5/RD-3): the driver's written statement [F9] asserts the rider said "ok" to going via Prince Charles Crescent on the 08:47 call [F8]. There is no in-app chat at all [F7] and no recording of the call; a verbal agreement needs the call recording, and a driver's statement that the rider agreed is a claim, not consent. The rider denies agreeing. Consent is therefore not established and no ground of exemption applies — the segment counts, and with no traffic reason this is also a driver violation under RD-2.

Amount (RD-2): refundable km × this trip's per-km distance fare. The excess distance fare is given as $4.08 (2.89 km × $1.4101/km) [F4]; the small difference between the code's 2.58 km segment figure and the 2.89 km billed is not separately exempt under RD-3/RD-5, so the full $4.08 excess is refundable. Tolls, time fare, booking/platform fee and surge [F5][F6] are not refunded; surge is 1.0× so no SURGE issue arises.

Remedies: refund_partial of $4.08 (excess distance fare only), plus the RD-7 reminder to the driver on notification duty and a log on his route-compliance record — no formal warning, as this is a first notification-related incident. No RD-6 flag: driver profile shows 0 upheld disputes in 90 days [F16], and the profile cannot decide the case anyway. Under TH-1/TH-2 an amount under $10 is a final system ruling (DISP-001, C1); a similar precedent is DISP-2026-0089 (uninformed reroute, $3.20). Safety screen: chat/statement/complaint contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — nothing to escalate.

segment_findings.reason: Off-route segment 08:59–09:06 drove 4.50 km vs 1.92 km optimal, +2.58 km. The only consent evidence is the driver's post-trip statement [F9] that the rider said 'ok' on the 08:47 call [F8]; there is no recording (RD-5 requires the call recording for verbal notice) and no in-app chat [F7], and the rider denies agreeing. No traffic reason either: F10's band-2 congestion is on Ayer Rajah Expressway, which the substituted roads do not replace, F11/F12 show the recommended roads flowing and F13 records no incident (RD-4). The segment therefore counts under RD-2.

element_findings.element: Verbal notice / consent on the pre-pickup call (RD-5)
element_findings.reason: The only evidence of consent is the driver's post-trip statement [F9] that the rider said 'ok' on the 08:47 call [F8]. A driver's word is a claim, not consent; verbal notice requires the call recording, and there is no recording on record and no in-app chat [F7]. The rider denies agreeing. Consent after/at the start of the segment is therefore not proven.

Band-2 congestion [F10] sits on Ayer Rajah Expressway, a road the recommended route does not use and which the driven segments did not replace; Central Expressway and Kent Ridge Road were in bands 7 and 5 [F11][F12], and no incident is recorded near the route [F13]. No traffic reason for the substituted segment.

element_findings.element: Driver's stated reason for the reroute
element_findings.reason: The driver's own words [F9] cite an AYE jam and say he would go via Prince Charles Crescent — an errand of his choosing, with no traffic justification on the replaced part of the recommended route.

rejected_claims.reason: Post-trip driver statement asserting oral consent is a claim, not consent; unrecorded verbal notice cannot satisfy RD-5 and the rider denies agreeing.
Congestion on Ayer Rajah Expressway, which is not on the recommended route and is not the part of the route replaced by the driven segments — no RD-4 traffic reason for the deviation.
